title: Does a sheet-following robot skill trained on a rigid-sheet simulator survive a flexing sheet, sensing delay and actuator lag?
summary: The buildbot-cohold follow skill (impedance gains K, B and an integral term) was tuned by random search on a rigid-sheet plant with randomised sheet mass (6–23 kg), lift time, reference lag and feed-forward error, then tested on 1000 fresh episodes of a held-out plant: two rigid halves on a torsional spring, a first-order force actuator and delayed feedback. A policy passes if peak tilt ≤ 3°, final tilt ≤ 0.5° and the person's load stays under the NIOSH constant. On the training plant the tuned skills pass 81–82% of episodes (lag-limited ceiling); on the held-out plant they pass 0–11%, because the high gains they pick go unstable under delay. The buildbot-cohold nominal setting passes 61% then 26%. A skill tuned on the held-out plant passes 61–66% there and 67–72% back on the rigid one. Randomising the parameters a simulator has does not cover the dynamics it lacks. Delay (0–30 ms), actuator lag (5–50 ms), sheet stiffness (150–6000 N m/rad) and the pass thresholds are my ranges, not measurements; the second plant is my own planar model, not a second physics engine.
lede: does a sheet-following skill tuned on a rigid-sheet simulator survive a flexing sheet with delay? It passes 81% of episodes where it was tuned and 0-11% on the held-out plant; tuning on the held-out plant gives 61-66% there.
